build: TAP of the original Ocean cassette (643,155 bytes): a 701-byte boot program in the KERNAL's format, then Ocean's turbo loader reading 275 pages of 256 bytes: the loading tune, the loading picture and the whole of memory from $0400 to $FFFF, which holds both parts of the game

exclude: the screen memory and sprite pointers of video bank 3: the start-up at $9762 clears and redraws the screens before they are shown, so the loaded bytes are never displayed

Not a variable. The bytes $A9 $03 that follow a BIT opcode ($2C) in the music driver's commands at $A018, $A15D and $A288: the processor reads them as the operand of BIT and skips them, where an entry at the second byte reads them as LDA #$03. It is the idiom that lets two entries share one tail.

Entry point of part one. The attract mode jumps here at $95BC and the end of the intro sequence at $9740. It runs part_one_prepare ($9762), sets the CIA2 VIC bank ($94), clears sprite expansion and priority and the scroll column $02AE, switches sprites 0 and 1 on, sets the colour of sprites 0 to 3 to 3 and of sprites 4 to 7 to 8, copies 17 bytes of initial sprite registers from $15EA, sets Johnny's sprite pointers to $C4 and $C5, builds the opening screen with $0B3B, silences the SID, starts tune $1A and falls into the main loop.

Top of the main loop. Each time round it first checks the out-of-energy flag at $0206 (set when the energy or shield bar is empty): while walking (mode 0) that ends the game with MALFUNCTION and TOTAL POWER LOSS. Then it checks whether Johnny has reached the exit at the left end of the map ($047B), then does the per-frame work (scroll, input, messages, mode handler) and loops back here.

Not out of energy: tests whether the scroll column $02AE has reached $FC (the left end of the map, reached by scrolling left from column 0) with sprite 0 at X $39 or less, Y from $50 to $63 and Johnny facing left ($0296 = 3); if so the room is left (1,000 points, the picture screen, then the ending checks), otherwise it carries on to the per-frame body at $04E8.

Per-frame body of the main loop: if the frame flag at $02BE is clear it only runs $0580 and loops. Otherwise it clears the flag and, if the interrupt made a scroll step ($02BF), clears that flag and the scroll request $21. It checks F5 ($9B3A, back to the attract mode); while the frame counter $0306 is non-zero it decrements it and, in mode 0, runs the alarm, laser pickup, time and countdown checks ($1F94, $1FBD, $1FD8, $1F72, $201A, $2436); then it runs the input, enemy, column bonus, action select, column, jump, message, pause and guard routines in turn. Finally, when fire is pressed in mode 0, it runs the handler of the selected action through the table at $0675, which returns into the dispatch of the current mode's handler through the table at $43E8; otherwise it dispatches straight to the mode handler. Both return to $0580.

Return point of every pass and the idle branch: the mode handlers return here (the main loop pushes $057F), and the loop comes here directly while the frame flag is clear. It runs timed_event at $203A, which, while bit 3 of $0299 and $0212 are set and fewer than four messages wait, counts $02F8 down and ends the game at zero, and goes back to the top of the loop.
Turns the joystick state in $20 into edge flags: fire held ($0201), fire pressed this pass ($0202), direction held ($0203) and direction pressed this pass ($0204).
Not a variable. The bytes $A9 $05 after a BIT opcode in the commands at $A20D, which the processor skips; the entry one byte later reads them as LDA #$05.

Moves Johnny's two sprites up one pixel and decrements his saved height $0301, or does nothing when sprite 0's Y is below $40; it clears the scroll request $21. Every third step up (counted in $0205) it also runs walk_right_step, so the step goes up on a slant. It is one of the four per-direction steps the walk code calls through the table at $1C2E.

Moves Johnny's two sprites down one pixel, increments $0301 and clears the scroll request $21 (there is no limit test here: the floor probe in walk_collision_check decides whether the step runs). Every third step down (counted down in $0205) it also runs player_move_left, so the step goes down on a slant. Part of the per-direction walk steps.

Moves Johnny's sprites left one pixel, clearing the scroll request $21 and $0207, while sprite 0's X is $84 or more. Below $84 it still moves him when the scroll column $02AE is $FC (the left end of the map, where the exit is); otherwise it sets the scroll direction $21 to $01 (scroll the screen content right) instead of moving him.

Moves the player sprite pair one pixel to the right when sprite 0's X is below $E0, clearing the scroll request $21 and setting $0207 to 1; at the right edge it either stops (clears the walking flag $02ED, when the scroll column $02AE is $F3, the right end of the map) or sets $21 to $FF to have the screen scroll.
Short entry stubs that combine a vertical step ($05D0 or $05F8) with a horizontal one ($0613 or $063A) for the diagonal directions.
Four words (address minus one) of the action handlers, indexed by the selected action: JUMP, LASER, SEARCH, UTILISE.
Data at $0676 (f_0676): read by main_loop_frame.

Polls the keyboard for the SPACE key (key $3C) and, when it is newly pressed ($02FD holds it until release) and no message is being typed ($0209), steps the selected action ($02FC) down by one, wrapping from JUMP to UTILISE, rewrites the action label, queues message 7 (SWITCH), sets the mode to 0 and queues the prompt.

Copies the eight-character name of the selected action from the table at $06E1 into the panel text row at $C373, adding $20 to each letter to reach the panel's own character codes (blank maps to $F8).
Four eight-character action names, in the order JUMP, LASER, SEARCH, UTILISE, used for the panel label.

Sets up the raster interrupt system: sets the time-of-day clock to 3:00, disables CIA1's interrupts, writes $80 to both CIAs' control registers A (timer A stopped, time-of-day clock at 50 Hz), enables the raster interrupt, points the IRQ vector at $0738, sets the scroll value $22 to $10, acknowledges any pending VIC interrupt and enables interrupts.

Raster interrupt handler of part one. Saves the registers, acknowledges the VIC, counts $02 down through 1, 0 and 2, and dispatches by RTS through the table at $5BF0 to the handler for the band: $07A0 at line $F3, $085E at line 0 and $0767 at line $A3.

Part one's raster handler for the band that starts at line $A3, where the status panel begins (the previous handler set that line). Selects screen 0 and the character set, sets the multicolour colours and the fixed horizontal scroll $18, sets the next interrupt line to $F3, raises the frame flag at $02BE, runs one step of the message printer $0E48 when $0294 is set, and then runs the scroll step if one is wanted.

Tail of the $A3 handler (irq_panel_band): when the scroll direction $21 is non-zero it runs the scroll step $087B and sets $02BF to 1, then falls into the common exit at $0799, which every raster handler uses to restore X, Y and A and return.

Part one's raster handler for line $F3, below the panel. It sets the screen, colours and scroll register ($D016 from $22, $D011 from $02A1) that the next frame's playfield will use, sets the next interrupt for line 0, counts the frame counter $0306 up, runs the sound driver and, unless the pause flag $0217 is set, updates the clock.
Not a variable. The bytes $A9 $07 after a BIT opcode in the command at $A0EB, which the processor skips; the entry one byte later reads them as LDA #$07.

Part of irq_frame_bottom ($07A0), reached when the game is not paused: updates the on-screen clock. When the CIA1 time-of-day seconds differ from the last value drawn ($02BD) it redraws the digits and the colon, otherwise it only sets the colon's blink.
Reads the CIA1 time-of-day clock (hours, minutes, seconds) and writes the digits into the panel's clock characters.
Sets the clock's colon characters at $C2FD and $C325 to character $F8 or $38 depending on bit 3 of the tenths of seconds, making it blink.
Writes the four characters of one big clock digit (digit in A, position in Y) into the panel.
Part one's raster handler for line 0: only sets the next interrupt line to $A3.
Sets the CIA1 time-of-day clock to X hours and Y minutes, zero seconds and tenths, and redraws it.

Scrolls the playfield by two pixels in the direction given by the sign of $21 (negative is left): moves sprites 2 and 3, adjusts $22 (the horizontal scroll value) and, when it wraps, shifts the whole 40-column character map and colour map by one column.
Shifts every row of the character and colour maps one cell to the left (each row is 40 cells, 12 rows of each map), then goes to the column refill at $0A33.
Shifts every row of the character and colour maps one cell to the right (12 rows of each map), then goes to the column refill at $0A33.

After a scroll the new edge column is filled from the room's tile map. Scrolling left ($21 negative) it draws character column $02C1 (the scroll phase plus one) of tile column $02AE+10 into screen column 39, moving the scroll column on when the phase wraps past 3; scrolling right it draws character column $02AD of tile column $02AE into screen column 0 and steps the phase back, moving the scroll column back when it passes 0. It calls the tile draw at $0A92 and the column write at $0B00.
Fetches the three tile numbers of one map column from the room map tables at $4000, $4100 and $4200 (indexed by X) and stores their character data in the temporary column buffer at $02AF.
Looks up one tile's 16 characters (a 4 by 4 block at $5000 plus 16 times the tile number) and copies one column of four of them to the column buffer at $02AF.
Converts a tile number in A to its character data address: $5000 plus 16 times the number, in zero page $24/$25.

Writes the twelve characters in the column buffer at $02AF down one column of the screen map from $C050 (the column is A minus 1: A is 1 for the left edge and $28 for the right) and the matching colours, looked up in the table at $8448, down the same column of colour memory from $D850.

Redraws the whole playfield from the room's tile map, starting at the current scroll column: for each of the 10 tile columns and 3 tile rows it expands the tile's characters into the screen map at $C050.

Second half of $0B3B: sets the scroll phase to $FF and fills the colour map at $D850 from the screen map at $C050, looking each character up in the colour table at $8448 (it reads each character with the undocumented opcode LAX, which loads A and X together).
Three screen-map pointers, $C050, $C0F0 and $C190: the start of each of the three tile rows of the playfield.
Three pointers, $4000, $4100 and $4200, to the three rows of part one's map; $0B3B reads them.
Data at $0BF1 (f_0BF1): read by build_screen.

Handler for the SEARCH action (entry 2 of the table at $0675, run when fire is pressed). Does nothing unless mode 0 is active and no message is queued; otherwise it finds what is at the player's position with $0D62 and, unless the search is refused ($02D6 negative: Johnny too low on the screen, not facing up, or no searchable tile there), queues message 0 (EXAMINE) and message 11 (PROCESSING), sets a delay of 100 passes and starts mode 1.

Second half of the mode 1 handler (search in progress; the first half at $0C20 aborts on a stick press): counts the delay at $02D4 down; at zero it reports the result: a locked container ($0DCA) gives MALFUNCTION and LOCKED and clears the mode, nothing found gives FOUND NOTHING and clears the mode, otherwise it queues FOUND and the name of each object found, moves to mode 2 and queues the prompt.
Sets the mode ($0200) to 0 and queues message 10, the prompt arrow.
Queues message 10, the prompt arrow, and returns.
Computes the map column under Johnny from sprite 0's X position, the scroll phase and the scroll column, and stores it in $021B.

Looks up what is at the player's map column. The search is refused ($02D6 = $FF) when sprite 0's Y is $62 or more (too low), when Johnny is not facing up ($0297 not 0), or when the tile in the map's middle row at that column is not one of the 43 in the table at $153D. Otherwise it clears the scroll request $21, sets the layer $02D5 to 3 and scans the object table at $1568 for records with that column and layer, collecting each one's object number into the list at $02D7 and its description number into $02DB; the count goes in $02D6.
Tests whether the container at the player's column is one that needs a key ($15BC), and whether its open flag in $020B is set; returns the carry set if it is still shut.
Queues the message number in A (without adding an offset).
Queues system message A, adding $0B so that 0 is PROCESSING (message 11).
Queues the object name for object number A, adding $35 to reach its text (object 0 is LASER ROM, message 53).
Queues the description message A, adding $4B to reach its text (description 0 is message 75).
Appends the message number in A to the message queue at $02C4 and bumps the queue length.
Starts printing the message at the head of the queue: finds its text in the message table at $0EBF by counting '!' terminators, and resets the print position.

Per-pass message printer: if nothing is printing it starts the next queued message; otherwise every third call it handles one more character of the text: '!' ends the message, '2' scrolls the window up a line and goes on at its second column, a space only moves on, '3' draws the prompt arrow (characters $7B and $7C at $C360) and ends the message, and any other character is written to the window's bottom row at $C360 with $20 added.

Ends the current message: shifts the queue at $02C4 down one entry, clears the printing flag $0209, scrolls the message window up a line ($1C90) unless the message was 10 (the prompt), and decrements the queue length.

Game text, messages 0 to 52, each ended by '!' ($21). Letters, digits and space are plain ASCII ($41 to $5A for A to Z); the printer adds $20 to reach the panel font. '2' ($32) is a line break and '3' ($33) draws the prompt arrow and ends the message. Messages 0 to 9 are the menu words (EXAMINE to NO), 10 is the prompt arrow, 11 onwards the system messages, 45 to 48 the endings, 49 the copyright, 50 and 51 the part headings and 52 the high-score prompt.
Continues text_messages ($0EBF to $12A0) at offset 321: Game text, messages 0 to 52, each ended by '!' ($21). No instruction names this address, the data is reached through an index or pointer.
Messages 53 to 88: the names of the 21 objects (53 to 73), a blank (74), and the descriptions (75 to 88) shown by DESCRIBE, each ended by '!'.
The 43 tile numbers that SEARCH accepts as something to search: $0D62 compares the tile in the room's middle row at the player's column with these.

The 21 objects, four bytes each: map column, layer (3 in every record, the layer the search sets in $02D5), object number and description number. Taking an object zeroes its column and layer; hiding one writes the player's map column ($021B) and layer ($02D5) into it; reset_game_state ($2421) rewrites every column from $260F and every layer as 3.

The layer byte of each object record (see $1568), reached by index: zeroed when an object is taken (the take step of modes 3 and 4, $0CED), written by mode_hide_do ($17C3) and reset_game_state ($2429); read by find_objects_here ($0DAD).
Data at $156A (f_156A): read by find_objects_here.
Data at $156B (f_156B): read by find_objects_here.
The map column of object 16, the LIGHTED CIGARETTE (0 while Johnny holds it), the first byte of its entry in the object table at $1568: check_cigarette_in_bin reads it.

The map column of object 20, the IGNITION KEY (the first byte of its record in $1568), $0D at the start. check_time_limit reads it at $1F82: once it is no longer $0D (the key has been taken or hidden elsewhere), the truck driver's message and the alarm follow.

The eight map columns of the locked containers (drawers and cabinets), in the order of their bits in $15C4. The fourth, $9D, does not match the map: the tile there ($68) is not one of the searchable tiles at $153D, and the INPUT table at $15CC has the drawer at $9A instead, so the lock check at $1CFA, given $9A, reads past these eight bytes to $15D8.
One bit per container, 1 to 128, for the open and key flags at $020B and $020C.
Ten three-byte entries (map column, then the address minus one of its INPUT handler): the places where an object can be used with INPUT.
Data at $15CD (f_15CD): read by mode_input_do.
Data at $15CE (f_15CE): read by mode_input_do.
Seventeen start values copied to the VIC registers $D000 to $D010 at game start: the sprite positions and the high bits.
Adds the three bytes at $02EA, $02EB and $02EC to the 6-digit decimal score at $02E7 to $02E9 (decimal mode), then redraws the score digits.
Draws the three score bytes at $02E7 to $02E9 as six big digits into the panel's score box.
Draws one score byte as two big digits.
Writes the four characters of one two-by-two digit (digit in A, column in Y) into the panel screen.
The message numbers of the sub-menu verbs (HIDE is the first and needs none; then INPUT, DESCRIBE) as the utilise menu cycles.
Three words (address minus one) of the starting routines of the HIDE, INPUT and DESCRIBE sub-modes.
Data at $1665 (f_1665): read by mode_utilise_menu.

Handler for the UTILISE action (entry 3 of the table at $0675). With nothing queued it queues UTILISE, then NOTHING TO USE when Johnny holds nothing (message 15), else it shows FIRE TO with HIDE and enters mode 5.

Mode 5: a stick press queues NO (declining the verb on offer), then FIRE TO and the next verb of HIDE, INPUT and DESCRIBE, and after the last it queues ABORT and ends the mode; fire jumps through the table at $1664 to the setup of the verb on offer.
Mode 6: choose which held object to hide: a direction press moves to the next one, fire selects it and moves to mode 7.

Mode 7: after a delay of 100 passes it checks that the container at this column is unlocked and not full, then moves the chosen object from the inventory into the room's object table at the player's column and layer.
Mode 10: choose which held object to INPUT: a direction press moves to the next, fire selects it (kept in $02FF) and moves to mode 11.
Mode 11: after a delay of 100 passes it looks the player's column up in the terminal table at $15CC and jumps to that terminal's handler, or says NO EFFECT.
Mode 8: choose which held object to DESCRIBE; fire selects and moves to mode 9.
Mode 9: after a delay of 100 passes it queues the description text of the chosen object (description index plus 75) and returns to mode 0.

Handler for the LASER action. If a LASER ROM (object 0) is in the inventory it returns at once and nothing more happens here; without one, and with nothing queued, it queues MALFUNCTION and NEED MORE INPUT and the prompt.

Handler for the JUMP action. Without a JUMP ROM (object 2) in the inventory it queues MALFUNCTION and NEED MORE INPUT; with one, and no jump already under way, it starts a jump: it records Johnny's sprite 1 height and the stick, and begins the arc at $19A5.
Runs once a pass: while a jump is active it replays the stick direction held at take-off and moves both player sprites up, then down, by the values in the arc table at $19CA.
Fifteen vertical steps of the rise of a jump (20 pixels in all): jump_step subtracts them from the player sprites' Y in order on the way up and adds them back in reverse order on the way down.
Tests one key of the keyboard matrix. A is the key number (row times 8 plus column); returns carry set when it is held. Keeps the CIA ports restored afterwards.
The eight CIA1 port A values that select one keyboard column at a time.

Thirty-two entries indexed by the inverted stick and fire bits (bits 0 to 4 of CIA1 port A): each holds the direction number 0 to 10 in its low bits plus $10 for fire, and $FF for impossible combinations such as up plus down or left plus right, which read_joystick turns into 0.
Mode 0, walking: moves Johnny by the stick, changing his walk frame when the direction changes, and works the walk cycle and scroll start.
Writes the pair of sprite pointers of walk frame X into $C3F8 and $C3F9.
Sets the walk animation tick counter $0298 to 3.

Advances Johnny's walk animation while the walking flag $02ED is set: it counts the timer $0298 down and every fourth call steps the walk frame $0303 (1, 0, 1, ...) and rewrites the sprite pointers from the frame table for direction Y. While the flag is clear it only selects the frame table for direction Y and shows its current frame.

Points $2C/$2D at the frame table for direction Y (Y is twice the stick value minus one; the pointers are at $1C4C) and writes its current frame $0303 into the sprite pointers through $1B51; it does not reset the frame.
Writes the current pair of sprite pointers of the frame table to $C3F8 and $C3F9.

Looks up the screen character at Johnny's feet probe (offset from sprite 1's X and the saved height $0301 by the pair for direction Y in $1BC1) and lets him step only when that character and the one to its right are both $76; otherwise it clears the scroll request $21 and the walking flag $02ED and returns. When the floor is there it goes on to the contact test against sprite 2 ($1BD5), which, unless it stops him, runs the walk step for direction Y through the table at $1C2E and sets $02ED.

Ten pairs of X and Y offsets (20 bytes), indexed by twice the stick value minus one, that place the feet probe relative to sprite 1's X and the saved height $0301; the pairs for the unused stick values 3 and 7 are zero.
Data at $1BC2 (f_1BC2): read by walk_collision_check.
Tests whether the enemy sprites are near Johnny's sprite pair and whether the sprites are enabled, to decide whether he is stopped.
Returns the difference between the Y positions of sprite 2 and sprite 0.

Ten words (address minus one) of the walk steps, indexed by twice the stick value minus one: up $05D0, down $05F8, left $0613, right $063A, and for the diagonals the stubs at $065D to $066F that combine them. The entries for the unused stick values 3 and 7 are $0000.
The high bytes of the walk_step_table words at $1C2E, read at $1C20 by the walk-step dispatch at the end of sprite_contact_check.

Johnny's walk frame data: the facing (0 to 7, $FF for the unused stick values) for each stick direction at $1C42, which mode_walk turns towards; the pointers to the walk frame tables of each direction at $1C4C; the sprite pointer pairs of the eight facings at $1C60, which $1AF0 writes into $C3F8 and $C3F9; and the four-byte walk frame tables at $1C70 to $1C8F, which $1B51 writes.
Data at $1C4C (f_1C4C): read by set_frame_table.
Data at $1C4D (f_1C4D): read by set_frame_table.
Data at $1C60 (f_1C60): read by set_walk_frame_pointers, enemy_walk.
Data at $1C61 (f_1C61): read by set_walk_frame_pointers, enemy_walk.
Data at $1C7A (f_1C7A): read by overlay_actor_update.
Data at $1C86 (f_1C86): read by actor_0231_update and move_pair_right through their shared tail at $323E ($324A), and by move_pair_b5 ($3276).
Scrolls the message window up by one line: copies each of the four text rows up and blanks the last.
INPUT handler for a container with a key lock: sets the object numbers that open it and the messages to show, then goes to the shared check at $1CFA.

Shared lock check: finds the container at the player's column in $15BC. The right key ($02F0) opens it (sets its bit in $020B, adds 1,500 points and queues the opened message $02F1), unless it is already open (message $02F2) or jammed (MALFUNCTION and LOCK JAMMED). The other key ($02F3) jams the lock (sets its bit in $020C), is removed from the inventory and gives MALFUNCTION and KEY MESHED IN LOCK; any other object gives NO EFFECT.

INPUT handler of the terminal at map column $55: the PASSCARD (object 14) gives SECURITY CLEARANCE GIVEN and sets $0210 to $11; any other object takes the alarm path at $1DAC (shared with the time, position and exit checks): it sets the alarm flag $0211, queues ALARM HAS GONE OFF and, while $0212 is clear, sets the guard state $0219 to 1.

INPUT handler of the computer terminal at map column $6B: the object number picks the step. PASSWORD logs on (bit 0 of $0299), COMPUTER PROTOCOLS links up when logged on (bit 1), and once linked the SECURITY DOCUMENT toggles the general alarm (bit 2; 3,000 points the first time it is overridden) and the FIRE SYSTEM MANUAL toggles the sprinkler system (bit 3; 5,000 points the first time it is switched off), each followed by LOG OFF, which clears bits 0 and 1. Anything else, or a step out of order, gives NO EFFECT.
Copies the status panel's characters from $9100 and $91B4 into the panel screen at $C258 and $C30C and draws the score and clock.

Fills the colour map from a block of screen characters through the table at $9000 (the character colours), reading each character with the undocumented opcode LAX; part of the picture and panel drawing.

Drains the energy bar ($029A) by Y steps (none when Y is 0): each step increments the character of the bar's current cell (it goes $35, $36, $37) and, when it reaches $38, blanks the cell and moves to the next cell down; when the last cell empties it sets the out-of-energy flag at $0206.
The same drain for the second bar (the one labelled S), at $029B.

Called from the main loop in mode 0 when the frame counter $0306 allows, while the alarm flag $0211 is clear: when the units digit of the clock's minutes is zero and the IGNITION KEY's column at $15B8 is no longer $0D (it has been moved), it queues message 43 (DRIVER LOOKING FOR TRUCK KEY), reads the tenths register ($1F7E) and jumps to the alarm path at $1DAC.
Reads the CIA1 time-of-day tenths register, which also releases the clock latch.

Checks the security clearance at map column $63, while the alarm flag $0211 is clear and the column $021B is not $FF. Below column $63 it clears $0210 unless bit 0 is set. At or beyond $63 it keeps only bit 4 of $0210 (so a clearance, $11 from the PASSCARD at $1DA6, is spent on the first crossing); if bit 4 is clear, Johnny has crossed without clearance and it jumps to the alarm path at $1DAC.
If the player's column is at or beyond $95 and bit 2 of $0299 is set, it jumps to $1DAC.

The first time object 16, the LIGHTED CIGARETTE, has been left at map column $F8 (its column in the object table at $15A8 reads $F8; it starts at $D6), it awards 5000 points, sets $0212 and queues BIN IS ON FIRE and ALARM HAS GONE OFF. With the sprinkler system on (bit 3 of $0299) it also queues SPRINKLER SYSTEM ACTIVATED and FAULT IN CIRCUITRY, and timed_event will end the game; otherwise it zeroes $02F7 and records the clock's minutes in $02F6 so that check_countdown can count four minutes.
Counts minutes after the flag is set and starts the sequence at $0219 after four.
Fires the end-of-game routine at $225E when the timer reaches zero.
Converts a decimal digit in A into the panel character for it.
Runs the enemy walk step twice.
Moves the enemy robot pair (sprites 2 and 3) towards Johnny's height, with a small state machine in $0213 to $0216 for each step.
Sets the enemy step timer $0216 to 6.

Brings the enemy robot pair (sprites 2 and 3) on when both are off and the scroll column $02AE has just changed to a column listed at $21CB: when the column went up (walking right) it compares $02AE plus 10 and places the pair at the right edge (X $160); when it went down it compares $02AE and places them at the left edge (X 4). It never switches them off; enemy_walk does that at $2148, scroll_screen_step at $0899 and $08D7, and check_time_up at $24E2.
The four scroll columns at which $216F brings the enemy robot pair on (compared with $02AE, or $02AE plus 10 when walking right).

Polls the F7 key (key 3 of the matrix). While it is first pressed it freezes the time-of-day clock (reading and rewriting the hours register holds the clock) and waits in a loop for a second F7 press, then restores the tenths-of-seconds register to restart the clock and sets $0306 to 1.

End-of-part-one check made when the player walks into the exit area: needs four objects in the inventory; each of the four listed at $225A found adds 2000 points; if the hold is not full or any is missing it queues two messages (MALFUNCTION and MORE INPUT NEEDED FOR SURVIVAL) and returns with carry set.
The four object numbers needed to build the decoy robot at the end of part one.

Waits in a busy loop (about 0.06 s per pass, longer with the interrupts) draining the energy bar and the shield bar one step each until the out-of-energy flag at $0206 is set. It sets $0294 so the message printer runs from the interrupt meanwhile. Used by the failure endings.

Once per pass when the alarm state at $0219 is nonzero: decides from sprite 2's position whether the guard comes from the right (state 1) or the left (state 2), then every second pass calls the matching mover ($22D0 or $2333).

Brings on sprites 4 and 5, drawn together as a guard, at the right (X $160 and $164) and walks them left towards Johnny. When sprite 4 is less than $20 pixels to the right of Johnny's sprite 0 the guard catches him, whatever the height: it shows the capture frames ($EC and $ED when sprite 4 is $10 or more below him, otherwise $F0 and $F4) and jumps to the capture ending.
The same for sprites 6 and 7, which walk in from the left.
Queues the CAPTURED AND DEACTIVATED message and runs the energy drain loop to the end.
Moves sprites 4 and 5 two pixels left, flipping between walk frames from the table at $23F8.
Moves sprites 6 and 7 two pixels right, flipping between walk frames from the table at $23FC.
Two four-frame cycles of sprite pointers: $F1 to $F4 for the guard walking left, $E2 to $E5 for the guard walking right.
Data at $23FC (f_23FC): read by guard_left_animate, move_actor_pair.

Waits for the message queue to empty, zeroes the game's variables from $0200 to $0294, copies 13 start values from $2602 into $0295 onwards and refills the object table at $1568 from the 21 start columns at $260F, each set to layer 3.
When the scroll column is between $EC and $FB it tests the clock minutes; most of the time it sets the alarm state to 2, otherwise it awards 2000 points once.

Draws the picture screen: copies two blocks of 240 characters from $9268 and $9358 into the screen map at $C050 and $C140, then runs $1EC6 to fill the colour map from $D850 for those 480 characters through the colour table at $9000. While it does so the playfield's video memory value $029C is $04 (character set at $D000); it sets it back to $06 at the end.
Copies 16 bytes of start positions to the sprite registers, eight sprite pointers to $C3F8 and eight colours to $D027.
Sixteen start values for the sprite position registers ($24B9) followed by eight sprite pointers ($24C9) and eight sprite colours ($24D1) that $2498 loads.
Data at $24C9 (f_24C9): read by init_sprites.
Data at $24D1 (f_24D1): read by init_sprites.

Reads the time-of-day clock. At hour 3 with minutes below $30 it enables sprites 0 to 3 and 6 and 7 and returns carry clear; otherwise it leaves only sprites 6 and 7 on and returns carry set, meaning the thirty minutes are up.
End-of-part-one scene: waits on frame flag $02BE and walks sprites 6 and 7 to the left, changing frame every four pixels, and then moves sprite 0 and 2 to 7 left.
Gives 2000 points the first time the player's map column is between $3D and $FB.
Called when part one is won: adds 10000 points, then a bonus for the minutes and the seconds left, plays the walk-off scene and resets the game state.
Waits until the frame counter $0306 reaches $F0, then calls $AC8D until it returns zero, and clears the counter.
Thirteen start values for the variables from $0295 ($2602), then the 21 start columns of the objects ($260F) that $2400 loads.
Data at $260F (f_260F): read by reset_game_state.

Entry of part two: resets the game state, sets the VIC bank, colours Johnny's two sprites and places them (slots 0 and 1, X $80, Y $74 and $89), clears the scroll column, the screen and the event column, draws the upper scenery and the starting scenery, installs the interrupts, sets the clock to 6:00 and draws it and the panel, refills the shield bar, selects the LASER action, programs CIA2 timer A ($0DD0) and enables its NMI, sets the music speed flag $031B, starts tune $21 and falls into the part-two main loop.

Main loop of part two. When the energy is out ($0206) it starts the ending once (tune $13, the player's frames, YOUR ENERGY HAS RUN OUT) and about 255 frames later goes to the scores. It checks F5, waits for the frame counter $0306, and each frame runs the ground check, the walk and fire (unless the energy is out or $030E holds them), the actors, the frame tail, the scenery animations, the chase trigger, the blocking check and the pause key; at scroll column $F6 with Johnny's X at $FF it goes to the win sequence at $39F5.

Frame tail of part two: moves the jump paths ($2D3C), runs the hit flashes ($3BF1), the column events at $8930 (unless the chase pair has started), the animation counters, copies the sprite slots to the VIC and runs the message printer.
Installs part two's interrupt set-up: disables the CIA1 interrupts, enables the raster interrupt, selects screen 1 and sets the IRQ vector to $27A1 and the NMI vector to $2956.

Part two's raster handler. Saves the registers, acknowledges the VIC, steps the band counter at $02 through 2, 1, 0 and dispatches by RTS through the three-entry table at $27C8 to the handler for the band.
Three words (address minus one) of the part-two raster handlers, indexed by twice the band counter: 0 is $282E (line $F3), 1 is $2804 (line $A3), 2 is $27CE (line $61).
Data at $27C9 (f_27C9): read by part_two_irq.

Part two's raster handler for line $61: sets the lower playfield band's screen from $029E and scroll from $02A0 with the colours $09 and $05, shifts the rows once if $0247 is set, and sets the next interrupt line to $A3.
Restores A, X and Y and returns from the part-two raster interrupt.

Part two's raster handler for the band at line $A3: selects the panel's screen and colours with the fixed scroll $18, counts the frame counter $0306 up, runs a scroll step if $21 asks for one, and sets the next interrupt line to $F3.

Part two's raster handler for line $F3: sets the upper playfield band's screen (0), scroll ($029F) and colours for the next frame, runs the sound timer, updates the clock and sets the next interrupt line to $61.

One step of part two's sideways scroll: moves sprite slots 2 to 7 one pixel left ($2884), then adds $80 to $0248, whose carry raises the count of pending row shifts at $0247 that the lower band's handler works off.
Frees sprite slot X when its ninth X bit is clear, or clears the bit.

From slot X to slot 7, moves each active sprite slot one pixel to the left with the scroll, freeing a slot that leaves the left edge ($2873). Then it counts the lower band's fine scroll $02A0 down; when it reaches a character boundary it resets it to 7, starts CIA2 timer A (the NMI at $2956 shifts the colour rows and draws the new column) and shifts the eight screen rows from $C0F0 one place to the left.

Called from the NMI after each character of scroll: steps the scroll phase $02AD (the character column within a tile, 0 to 3, moving the scroll column $02AE on when it wraps) and draws the new right-hand character column: column $02AD of the tiles at map column $02AE plus 10 in the map rows at $4400 and $4500, through the row pointers in zero page $10 and $30.

Writes one character column of a tile of part two's scenery (tile number in A, column $02AD): its four characters, and their colours from $9448, go into four rows through the row pointers in zero page $10 and $30, starting at the row $02AB, which it then leaves at the next row.
Converts a tile number in A to its character data address, $4600 plus 16 times the number, in zero page $24 and $25.

Non-maskable interrupt handler of part two, driven by CIA2 timer A. If the serial-port bit is set it goes to $2B25; otherwise on a timer underflow it stops the timer (scroll_sprite_slots starts it again at the next character), enables interrupts, shifts the eight colour rows from $D8F0 one cell left and calls $28EC for the new column.

Scrolls the upper band of part two's scenery by a pixel: decrements its fine scroll $029F, and at a character boundary resets it to 7 and shifts the four screen rows from $C050 (rows 2 to 5) and their colour rows one character to the left, wrapping the first column to the end. Called from the line-$61 handler once for every two scroll steps, so the upper band moves at half the speed of the lower one.

Builds part two's whole starting scenery: expands ten tile columns, two tiles high, from the map rows at $4400 and $4500 (through the pointers at $2B21) into the screen map from $C0F0, sets the scroll phase $02AD to 0 and falls into the colour fill at $2AD4.

Fills part two's colour map at $D850 and $D8F0 from the characters on screen, looking each one up in the colour tables at $4320 (characters $80 up) and $9448, reading each character with the undocumented opcode LAX.
Copies the two 16-byte tables of row pointers from $5BD0 and $5BE0 into zero page $10 to $1F and $30 to $3F.
Two pointers, to the map rows at $4400 and $4500, used by $2A42.
Data at $2B22 (f_2B22): read by draw_part_two_screen.
Handles the CIA2 serial-port NMI source: re-programs timer A with a short count, waits a short loop, restores the serial data register and jumps to $0107.
Copies 160 bytes of screen data from $4300 into the top of the screen map at $C050.
Fills four 256-byte blocks of the screen map ($C000, $C100, $C200, $C2E8) with the blank character $F8.
Reads the joystick on CIA1 port A, inverts the five bits, and looks the result up in the table at $1A1B to get the direction in zero page $20 (a negative table entry gives 0).

Part two's player movement: finishes a turn in progress ($020F), or else takes the stick (the last bits in $20 while Johnny's jump path is active, otherwise read_joystick): no direction stops the walk; a sideways push that differs from his facing starts a turn; otherwise it dispatches through the table at $8FE8 by the four stick bits to the jump, duck and walk actions.

Part two's action for the stick pushed up: unless the sprite slots are already on a path ($026B), it starts slots 0 and 1 on the jump path and sets the jump frames: sprite pointers $A0 and $A1 when Johnny faces right ($0297 is 7), otherwise $A2 and $A3.
Part two's action for the stick pushed down: clears the walking flag, sets the duck frame choice from $0303, and falls into the duck step at $2C38.
Part-two duck: counts the duck timer $029D down, sets the duck sprite frame and starts the ducking animation; at zero it ends the duck.
Part two's action for the stick pushed left: if the walking flag $02ED is set, takes a left step ($2C81) and advances the walk frame.
Moves the player's two sprites one pixel left while slot 0's X is $40 or more (so down to $3F); below that it ends the walk (clears $02ED).
Part two's action for the stick pushed right: if the walking flag $02ED is set, takes a right step ($2CA4) and advances the walk frame for direction $0E (right) through walk_frame_advance.

Moves the player's two sprites one pixel right while slot 0's X is below $B0. Further right, from scroll column $F6 on it still moves him; before that it asks for a scroll step instead (increments $21), and while $030B is set (check_exit_blocked) and no jump path is active it also pushes him one pixel right.
Part two's stick action for up and left: turns Johnny to face left if he is not, otherwise runs the jump start and the left walk.

Part two's stick action for down and left: if Johnny is not facing left it starts the turn to the left and does nothing else; otherwise it runs the duck step and then a left step (the walk at $2C73 once $0221 is set, the bare step $2C81 before).
Part two's stick action for up and right: if Johnny is not facing right it starts the turn to the right and does nothing else; otherwise it takes a right step ($2CA4) and runs the jump start.

Part two's stick action for down and right: if Johnny is not facing right it starts the turn to the right and does nothing else; otherwise it runs the duck step and then a right step (the walk at $2C96 once $0221 is set, the bare step $2CA4 before).
Marks Y consecutive entries of the eight-slot shot tables, starting at X, as active and moving up.

Moves each active entry of the eight-slot table at $026B along a path read from $8FC8, advancing a step counter in $027B and switching direction in $0273 at step $20; an entry that has stepped back to zero is released.

Chooses the duck frame of Johnny's second sprite from the table at $2DBE, at Y (0 facing right, 2 facing left) plus the phase in $0220, and writes it to $C3F9. While the walking flag is set the phase toggles every fourth call ($0298); otherwise it stays as part_two_duck_start chose it.
Pointers of Johnny's second sprite while he ducks in part two: $F6 and $87 facing right, $F8 and $88 facing left, the two of each pair alternated by the phase in $0220.
Event routine: allocates a sprite for the entity in slot $0222 and colours it.

Event 1's creature (sprite slot in $0222; it enters from the left at height $70). Each pass it moves 3 pixels right ($3618 with carry set); when it leaves the world the slot variable is cleared and 80 points are added. While Johnny is not ducking ($0243 is 0) it hurts him when its X is 0 to 31 pixels beyond his (0 to 15 in the halved positions slot_x_position returns): the shield (carry set at $32C7) loses 3 steps, its slot variable is cleared and the hit flash frees its sprite later. Its frame comes from $8F9A and the animation counter $02A7.
Event 4: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $98 for the entity in slot $0223 and colours it 8.

Event 4's creature (slot in $0223; it enters from the right at height $98). Each pass it moves 1 pixel left; leaving the world clears the slot variable and adds 35 points. It hurts Johnny when its X is about 8 pixels behind to 15 pixels beyond his (-4 to 7 in the halved positions slot_x_position returns) and Johnny's second sprite is at height $87 or lower: the shield loses 4 steps. Its frame comes from $8FA7 and the counter $02A5.
Event 2: allocates a sprite at the right edge at height $8A for the entity in slot $0225 and colours it 1.

Event 2's creature (slot in $0225; it enters from the right at height $8A). Each pass it moves 3 pixels left; leaving the world clears the slot variable and adds 100 points. It hurts Johnny when its X is 2 to 32 pixels behind his (1 to 16 in the halved positions slot_x_position returns) and his second sprite is at height $7C or lower: the shield loses 6 steps. Its frame comes from $8F9E and the counter $02A6.
